raw_response:
I’m on 10.1 mu total, so I won’t spread myself too thin. The main land stays in wheat-maize rotation because that is the safest income here, and I’ll keep a smaller piece in cotton. I’ve farmed a long time, so I mostly follow what has worked on my own fields and what people around me do. Wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, so at the start of this season my main concern is topdressing and watering it at the right time. If the wheat stand looks even and the color is good, I won’t push fertilizer too hard because water and fertilizer both cost money. But I also don’t dare underfeed it too much, because losing wheat yield hurts more than spending a bit extra on urea.

For maize, the key is speed after wheat harvest. Around here the turnaround is tight, so I will harvest wheat, clear the field quickly, and plant maize right away, with simple tillage or rotary tillage so I don’t miss moisture. I’ll use hybrid maize seed because saved seed is too risky for yield. Cotton I’ll keep on a smaller plot. Cotton needs more watching and more hand labor for picking, and with some family members working off-farm, I cannot put too much land into it. I’ll still plant it because it spreads risk. If grain prices are weak or weather turns bad, cotton gives me another income line. I’ll use moderate fertilizer on cotton, not the highest rate, and irrigate only when it really needs it because pumping from the well is not cheap.
